steps.description: Parse binary STL file — read header, triangles, and extract Material ID from Attribute Byte Count

suggestions: Binary STL format: 80-byte header, 4-byte triangle count, then per-triangle: 12-byte normal + 3×12-byte vertices + 2-byte attribute.
Extract Material ID from the 2-byte Attribute Byte Count field of each triangle.
warnings: Do not use numpy-stl or mesh library for reading — they may discard the Attribute Byte Count field that stores the Material ID.

steps.description: Build connectivity graph — identify connected components by triangle adjacency (shared edges)
Filter the largest connected component — remove scanning debris (small spurious triangles)

suggestions: Select the component with the most triangles as the main scan body; discard all others as scanning artifacts.

steps.description: Calculate volume by summing signed volumes of all triangles using the divergence theorem

suggestions: Signed volume of a triangle: V_i = (v1 · (v2 × v3)) / 6. Sum over all triangles and take absolute value.
The divergence theorem approach works for watertight meshes.

steps.description: Look up density from material_density_table.md by matching the extracted Material ID
Compute mass = volume × density and save results to mass_report.json
